entry.title: Stephanie Tranquille v New Beginnings Network [2026] FWC 4113
entry.content:
This was an application by New Beginnings Network to vary an unfair dismissal compensation order so that it could pay $5,025 by instalments of $50 per week, citing financial hardship. The Fair Work Commission refused the amount sought but varied the order to allow 10 weekly instalments of $502.50, with superannuation payable on the original due date.

Key holding: Under s 393 of the Fair Work Act 2009 (Cth), the Commission has a broad discretion to permit unfair dismissal compensation to be paid by instalments, exercised by weighing the respondent’s business needs and likely compliance against the applicant’s need to access compensation within a reasonable period.

In McCarron, James v Commercial Facilities Management Pty Ltd T/A CFM Air Conditioning Pty Ltd [2013] FWC 3577 in ordering that compensation be paid in instalments Bissett C said that when considering the time period for the instalment payments to be made the business needs of the Respondent must be weighed against the needs of the Applicant to access the compensation.

entry.title: VBCW and Commissioner of Taxation (Practice and procedure) [2026] ARTA 2312
entry.content:
This was an interlocutory tax review proceeding in the Administrative Review Tribunal. The Applicant sought to amend his Statement of Facts, Issues and Contentions and to expand his grounds of objection concerning trust distributions, Division 40 deductions, balancing adjustment events, and management fees allegedly deductible under s 8-1 of the ITAA 1997. The Tribunal granted leave to amend and exercised the para 14ZZK(a) TAA discretion to allow the expanded objection grounds.

Key holding: The Tribunal has a discretion under para 14ZZK(a) of the Taxation Administration Act 1953 (Cth) to allow a taxpayer to expand the grounds of objection beyond those originally stated.

The Tribunal exercises its discretion in paragraph 14ZZK(a) of the Taxation Administration Act 1953 (Cth) to allow the Applicant to expand his grounds of objection to cover the matters set out at paragraph 95-97 of the Applicant's Statement of Facts, Issues and Contentions.

entry.title: Carbery v Fire Rescue Victoria [2026] FCA 1488
entry.content:
The Federal Court determined a separate question in three related proceedings concerning the fringe benefits tax treatment of contributions reimbursed by Fire Rescue Victoria to firefighters who are members of an income protection scheme. Justice McElwaine held that the apportionment methodology adopted by FRV was reasonable and fair, and answered that the taxable value of member contributions for the period 1 January 2023 to 1 October 2025 was 28.4% inclusive of GST.

entry.title: Ms Rebecca Long v Commonwealth Of Australia As Represented By The Commissioner Of Taxation Trading AS Australian Taxation Office [2026] FWC 2583
entry.content:
Ms Long applied under s.739 for the Commission to deal with a dispute about flex time and return-to-work meetings under the ATO Enterprise Agreement 2024. The Commission found that the return-to-work meeting issue was not a matter arising under the Agreement, and that the union had not complied with the cl.109 dispute resolution procedure because genuine discussions with relevant managers, including workplace relations managers, had not occurred.

Fair Work Commission, 7 Jul 2026, [2026] FWC 2583

entry.title: James (Gemma) Moore v Bytewize Pty Ltd [2026] FWC 1860
entry.content:
Following a finding that Gemma Moore's dismissal by Bytewize Pty Ltd was unfair, the Commission assessed compensation in lieu of reinstatement. Applying the Sprigg formula, it found she would have remained employed for a further 5.5 weeks (about $9,974.19 gross including superannuation), deducted amounts earned and likely to be earned (about $5,568.14), and ordered compensation of $4,406.05 gross less taxation.

entry.title: Ms Samantha Corneille v Salama Tea House [2025] FWC 3748
entry.content:
Ms Corneille applied for an unfair dismissal remedy 23 days after her dismissal took effect, outside the 21-day limit. She sought an extension of time citing health issues, computer illiteracy and having contacted Centrelink and the ATO before lodging. The Commission was not satisfied there were exceptional circumstances and dismissed the application, having proceeded in her absence.

Fair Work Commission, 8 Dec 2025, [2025] FWC 3748

entry.title: Artisan Pools Pty T/A Northern Rivers Pools v Mr Anthony Mutton [2025] FWC 2982
entry.content:
Artisan Pools sought a stay of the compensation order made by Commissioner Sloan after Mr Mutton's successful unfair dismissal application, pending appeal. Vice President Gibian found the appeal arguable but not strong and held the balance of convenience did not favour a stay, since there was no evidence that repayment would be impossible or that payment would cause immediate financial difficulty. The stay application was refused.

Fair Work Commission, 7 Oct 2025, [2025] FWC 2982

entry.title: Australian Municipal, Administrative, Clerical and Services Union v Commonwealth of Australia as represented by the Commissioner of Taxation [2025] FWC 2668
entry.content:
The ASU brought a s.739 dispute alleging the ATO breached freedom of association provisions in its enterprise agreement by dealing directly with a member (Mr Singh) about his flexible work request while the ASU was representing him. The Commission found the ATO did not fail to act in good faith under cl.12.2, but did fail to respect and facilitate the ASU's role as representative under cl.12.4 when a manager arranged a direct meeting with Mr Singh.

Fair Work Commission, 9 Sep 2025, [2025] FWC 2668
